## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

Passage-level parallels are attested in the *Udānavarga* tradition, specifically within the *Paśyavarga* (UV 27, Sanskrit UVS 27, and Tibetan Uv Kg 27) [SuttaCentral]. The text is also cited in early paracanonical and exegetical treatises, including the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 15 *Otaraṇahāravibhaṅga* and Ne 37 *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) and the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2 *Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi* and Pe 8 *Hārasampātabhūmi*) [SuttaCentral].
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the sutta exhibits 53 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 10 canonical works [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial overlap is with the immediately following *Dutiyalakuṇḍakabhaddiya Sutta* (Ud 7.2), sharing an extensive section (§1.1–4.1 with Ud 7.2 §1.1–3.1) [DharmaNexus]. Other significant formulaic and narrative correspondences occur with the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), the *Ānandabhaddekaratta Sutta* (MN 132), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1) and *Cīvarakkhandhaka* (Kd 8), as well as selections from the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3, AN 4) and elsewhere in the *Udāna* (Ud 1.5, Ud 3.2, Ud 8.1) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
